class.name: ESCData
class.description: Assign to [member VehicleConfig.esc_data] to enable ESC. The assigned resource is observed once per physics tick; edits and removal take effect on the next tick. Replacement resets the output history. The controller compares actual yaw rate with a bicycle-model steering target and applies bounded chassis torque. It requires at least two grounded wheels and the configured minimum forward speed. With smoothing disabled the raw controller preserves the previous aerodynamic yaw-control behavior. ESC is sampled once per physics tick before steering/tire substeps. Support loss, disabling, invalid observations, resource replacement and restart reset torque immediately. Normal speed-gate release uses the configured slew rate. Nonpositive/nonfinite dt returns zero without advancing history.

members.member: Enable yaw correction. False applies no corrective torque.
Yaw-rate feedback gain. Torque is negative estimated yaw inertia times this gain times actual-minus-target yaw rate.
Minimum absolute chassis forward speed for intervention, in m/s.
Maximum absolute corrective chassis yaw torque, in Nm.
Target lateral acceleration ceiling, in m/s^2. Limits target yaw rate to this value divided by absolute forward speed (with a 1 m/s denominator floor).
Enable separate output engagement/release slew limits. Disabled by default for baseline comparison pending driving calibration.
Maximum growth of torque magnitude, in Nm/s. Finite and positive. Ramp duration is absolute torque change divided by this rate. Provisional tuning value; does not lower the steady torque ceiling.

Maximum reduction of torque magnitude, in Nm/s. Finite and positive. Sign reversal releases to zero then engages with the remaining time in the same tick. Lowering the torque cap takes effect immediately.
